title: Paneer Tikka Masala Bowls
seoTitle: Paneer Tikka Masala Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Seared paneer in a creamy tomato masala sauce over basmati rice
subtitle: Seared paneer in a creamy tomato masala sauce over basmati rice
description: Cubes of paneer sear until golden, then simmer in a spiced tomato-yogurt masala sauce over basmati rice. It is a genuine curry-night option for vegetarian crew members that still lands a real per-serving protein count.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse basmati rice and cook according to package directions. Fluff and hold covered.

steps.title: Sear the paneer
steps.instruction: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Sear paneer cubes in batches, 2–3 minutes per side, until golden. Remove and set aside — do not crowd the pan.

steps.title: Build the masala base
steps.instruction: In the same pan, cook onion 5–6 minutes until soft, then add garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute more. Stir in garam masala, cumin, and turmeric and toast 30 seconds.

steps.title: Simmer the sauce
steps.instruction: Add crushed tomato and simmer 12–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened and deep red.

steps.title: Finish off heat
steps.instruction: Remove the pan from heat, then stir in greek yogurt and heavy cream until smooth — adding dairy off heat keeps the sauce from breaking.

steps.title: Return the paneer
steps.instruction: Fold seared paneer back into the sauce and warm gently over low heat 3–4 minutes, just until heated through.

steps.title: Serve over rice
steps.instruction: Spoon paneer tikka masala over basmati rice and finish with fresh cilantro if using.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover paneer tikka masala — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool paneer tikka masala and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Pat paneer dry before searing so it browns instead of steaming.
Rookie tip: Stir dairy in off heat and over low, gentle warming only — a hard boil after adding yogurt can curdle the sauce.
Add frozen peas in the last few minutes for extra color and volume.
tonightSpread: Sides: Cucumber raita, simple green salad
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool paneer tikka masala in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Reheat gently over low heat with a splash of water so the sauce doesn't break.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It gives vegetarian crew members an actual curry-night entrée instead of a side dish, and the sauce is rich enough that nobody misses the chicken.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: the masala sauce improves overnight in the fridge. Storage: keep paneer-in-sauce and rice in separate containers up to 4 days. Reheating: reheat sauce gently over medium-low so the paneer doesn't turn rubbery from a hard boil.
substitutions: Use extra-firm tofu instead of paneer for a dairy-free-adaptable version (still contains dairy in the sauce unless yogurt/cream are swapped).
Use coconut milk instead of heavy cream and yogurt for a dairy-free sauce.
Use brown rice instead of basmati for more fiber.
